description_full: Sirius XM Holdings Inc. operates as an audio entertainment company in North America. It operates through two segments, Sirius XM, and Pandora and Off-platform. The Sirius XM segment provides music, sports, entertainment, comedy, and talk and news channels, as well as podcast and infotainment services on subscription fee basis; and live, curated, and exclusive and on demand programming services through satellite radio systems and streamed through applications for mobile and home devices, and other consumer electronic equipment. This segment also distributes satellite radios through automakers and retailers, as well as its website; offers advertising other ancillary services; sells radios and accessories; and offers location-based services through two-way wireless connectivity, including safety, security, convenience, maintenance and data, remote vehicles diagnostic, and stolen or parked vehicle locator services, as well as data services related to graphical weather and fuel prices. In addition, this segment provides music channels on the DISH Network satellite television service as a programming package; Travel Link, a suite of data services that include graphical weather, fuel prices, sports schedule and scores, and movie listings; graphic information related to road closings, traffic flow, and incident data for consumers with in-vehicle navigation systems; real-time weather services in vehicles, boats, and planes; music programming and commercial-free music services for office, restaurants, and other business; and wireless communications service. The Pandora and Off-platform segment operates music, comedy, and podcast streaming platform, which offers personalized experience for listener through mobile devices, vehicle speakers, and connected devices; and provides advertising services. The company was incorporated in 2013 and is headquartered in New York, New York.

financial_summary: SiriusXM Holdings Inc. is a large-cap communication services business with a $10.7B market cap on $8.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -2% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 26% against a 7% cost of capital — a 19-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 55% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $1.2B in free cash flow — roughly 15 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.36× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.5× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and interest coverage runs at 3.2×.

Shareholder yield of 4.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 46% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

AI-generated content commoditisation — as creation costs collapse toward zero, content libraries lose pricing power and differentiation narrows.

sect: Its 17% operating margin runs 9pp above the Communication Services median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.84x).
It accounts for 0.4% of sector revenue and 0.3% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-3.3% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.06 across 171 companies in the universe; the top four hold 36% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 27% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 6% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 33% and a beta of 1.00, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.38 vs 5y 1.00), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $108.2M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 40% in the 2020 crash, 16% in the 2022 bear market and 98% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 42% below its DCF fair value of $54.47, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 35%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $34.49 to $85.47 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Communication Services peers: EV/EBITDA 7.9 vs 9.9 and P/FCF 8.6 vs 11.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 15% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 11.6% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 7.4% (vs the 8% bar).
The 13 covering analysts target $34.31 on average, 8% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 26% clears the cost of capital of 7.1% by 19pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.58).
It runs a 55% gross margin and converts 15% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 2.36x.
ROE of 7% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.4x equity multiplier).
It spends 3.1% of revenue on R&D and 2.1% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 4.5x net debt to EBITDA ($94.0M of cash against $8.6B of debt), with interest covered 3.2x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 1.39 in the distress zone.
The current ratio of 0.30 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
Goodwill makes up 45% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -1.7% over 3 years, 1.3% over 5 years and 6.5% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded -5.7% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex runs 1.5x depreciation (7.6% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
Its Rule of 40 score is 14, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 46.0%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 53%.
Insider trading is two-way: 3 purchases and 2 sales over the past year, net $25.8M bought.
It returns 4.7% a year to shareholders (1.3% in buybacks and 3.4% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 3.2% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 10 consecutive years, raising it 13.7% a year over the last five.
Short interest is elevated at 14.9% of the float, 6.8 days to cover.
people: With about 5,119 employees, each generates about $1.7M of revenue, 2.7x the Communication Services median, and revenue has grown 7.7% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $243K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $8.0M (5x revenue per employee).
